headline: This law changes how the VA and its appeals board handle veterans' disability claims based on military sexual trauma, including training, letter wording, and exam practices.
what_it_does: The law requires the VA to offer annual training on military sexual trauma (MST) to each member of the Board of Veterans' Appeals, and bars assigning MST-related cases to members who have not completed it. When an appeal is filed and the veteran asks for a hearing, the board must quickly decide whether the case involves an MST-related claim. The VA must also review and revise letters that explain denied MST claims so they use trauma-informed language and avoid wording that could retraumatize veterans. Finally, the VA must set up protocols so that VA and contract medical examiners use trauma-informed methods when examining veterans for MST-related claims.

who_it_affects.group: Veterans who have filed claims for disability compensation based on military sexual trauma
who_it_affects.how: Their appeals may be routed to trained board members, their hearing requests are flagged for quick review, and denial letters and medical exams are expected to follow trauma-informed practices.

who_it_affects.group: Members of the Board of Veterans' Appeals
who_it_affects.how: They must be offered annual training on MST and related proceedings, and they cannot be assigned MST cases until they complete it.

who_it_affects.group: VA medical providers and contract medical providers who perform claim-related exams
who_it_affects.how: They must follow new VA protocols that call for trauma-informed practices when examining veterans for MST-related claims.

who_it_affects.group: VA staff who write claim decision letters
who_it_affects.how: Their letters on denied MST claims must be audited and revised to use trauma-informed language.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted December 27, 2022; the summary does not list specific deadlines for each requirement.
